scope.exceptional_witnesses: Sections 2-4 and Appendices A-C: polynomial regularity, subgroup invariance, purity, row degrees, factorial denominators, Wilson congruence, Klein identities, Cartier pullback and nonzero binary coefficients.
scope.radial_witness: Section 5: independently derived all-order binomial cancellation of pure moments, positive double-integral formula and triangle evaluation for marked moments, normalizer invariance and explicit radius scaling. The new printed formulas were reread against that derivation.
scope.connected_classification: Section 6: compact forms including disconnected stabilizers, line/doublet construction, regular dual matrix coefficients, branching rules, proper SL2 stabilizer images and subdirect products.
scope.disconnected_classification_and_nullcone: Section 7: number-field specialization, completely splitting primes, exponent separation, Newton identities, component averaging and the character-lattice criterion. Finite spaces, inversion and factor-permutation examples were also checked.
scope.recompositions: Section 8: CRT choice of a fixed marker, valuation extension with unit coefficients, unique negative valuation, descent of algebraicity, finite-generation Eisenstein argument and prime-quotient reduction for coefficient algebras.
scope.primary_source_dependencies: All 15 current bibliography entries have inspected supporting passages and recorded scope, including the two missing Long references.
scope.proof_clarifications: The exact fixed subspace, representation-coordinate invariant, Cartier scalar cancellation and separable field inclusion were reread after revision; theorem scope is unchanged.

title: Counterexamples to the Mathieu Property: From Explicit Quotient Constructions to a General Classification

novelty_comparison.already_established: Long's SU(2) counterexample, compact connected group classification, universal radial transfer and connected spherical classification.
novelty_comparison.additional_scope_here: Explicit right-invariant witnesses on the exceptional nonspherical quotients SL2/2O and SL2/2I, the resulting classification without sphericity, and disconnected acting groups.
novelty_comparison.essential_obstacle: A group counterexample need not descend to a finite right quotient. Averaging the pure function introduces mixed products with uncontrolled moments.
novelty_comparison.alternative_proof: Section 5 supplies a different radial pair and closed marked-moment formula, not new existence of radial transfer.

review_response.finding: Missing Long SU(2) and compact connected group attribution
review_response.resolution: Introduction and two bibliography entries give exact theorem citations before presenting the extension; Section 5 separately credits prior radial transfer.
Introduction explains required right invariance and uncontrolled mixed moments under averaging.

review_response.finding: Lemma 6.3 needs the entire fixed subspace
review_response.resolution: The alternating tensor explicitly spans V^{H0}; normality preserves this full one-dimensional space.
The proof defines the K-module W, its coordinate functions z_i and their product in C[W]^K, with values one at the tuple and zero at the origin.

review_response.finding: Cartier scalar and field inclusion compressed
review_response.resolution: Section 4 states -v is in Fp*, names the intermediate cubic field E and its separable inclusion, and uses Fp-linearity to cancel the scalar.

review_response.finding: Central coefficient mechanism compressed in overview
review_response.resolution: The introduction explains Haar coefficient reduction, the Klein map to a cubic, Cartier pullback and the nonzero binomial coefficient; Section 4 identifies the affine coefficient by homogeneity.
The abstract states that each exceptional pair has one fixed multiplier for all recompositions of each prescribed positive degree, independently of coefficients, as already proved in Theorem 8.1.
